assessment: The incumbent appears adequate under stable assignments: 24 such files had seven-minute median handling, while execution took only 40–75 seconds. Change-related selection or interpretation is a plausible weakness, not an established cause. The two renamed-course cases limit an instructor-assignment-only account. Zero observed cross-center rows provides bounded reassurance; the excluded course-split center remains untested. The overall 32/40 intended-course rate and 17-minute median miss the targets.

openings.claim: Reconstructing a requested week using current assignments or mutable course names may explain affected exports. Stable course identity plus week-relevant membership could improve correctness within the existing exporter.
openings.delta: Test temporal membership and identity interpretation before changing scheduling or export infrastructure; treat assignment changes, renames, and splits as distinct cases.
openings.prediction: Against coordinator-confirmed weekly expectations, current-state selection will differ from week-relevant selection after assignment changes; rename-only discrepancies will distinguish missing rows from name-based recognition failures.
openings.probe: Use fabricated staging courses for unchanged assignments, midweek reassignment, rename, and split. Compare course identities and participant rows in the documented CSV with agreed expected sets, including foreign-center negative controls. Keep attendance entry available. Estimate history availability and implementation effort before selecting a change within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Weekly expectations can be reconciled despite differing timetables.
Historical membership may need reconstruction; feasibility is unverified.

openings.claim: Which coordinator actions drive the handling-time excess, and does replacement waiting consume active work or mainly elapsed time?
openings.delta: Separate checking, correction, download, import, and follow-up effort instead of treating short job runtime or long replacement delay as the handling-time cause.
openings.prediction: If identity reconciliation dominates, affected cases will show excess checking and correction minutes. If replacement coordination dominates, excess active time will concentrate in requests and follow-ups; unattended waiting alone will not explain active handling.
openings.probe: Use the two short sessions with six consenting coordinators to time these phases on fabricated unchanged and changed-course examples using the existing CSV workflow. Record only phase durations and discrepancy types, with no participant names leaving authorized environments.
assumptions: Active handling and elapsed waiting are measured separately.
Short staged sessions may not represent all eight centers or production weeks.
